Alright, let me sit down and think through the year. It's early spring — wheat is already in the ground from last October, cotton goes in next month, and maize comes right after wheat harvest in June. Thirty years of doing this, and honestly I don't change much year to year unless I have a reason.

**How I split my 7.8 mu**

Same as last year and the year before. About 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation on the better piece near the well. The other 2.8 mu — that strip further out along the road — I put in cotton. Water's harder to get to that strip and cotton doesn't need as much. Cotton also brings in cash at a different time of year than the grain, so if grain prices are bad one side, maybe cotton carries us. My wife and I can just about handle 2.8 mu of cotton by ourselves for picking. Any more and I'd have to hire hands, and then the money goes out instead of staying home.

**Wheat (5 mu) — already planted last October**

I put in Jimai 22, same variety as the village coop sold everyone. About 25-30 jin per mu of seed, maybe 80 yuan a mu. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, 40-kg bags, around 150 yuan a bag. That's what Old Zhang down the road does, that's what I do. I watered once before freeze-up to help them through the winter.

Now that spring is here, I'm watching for jointing — probably early April. That's when I topdress with urea. I'll put down about half a bag per mu, so 20 kg. If the wheat looks pale I might bump it up to 25 kg. If we've had good rain and the leaves are dark green, I hold off a bit — no sense wasting fertilizer money when the crop doesn't need it. I'll irrigate at jointing, and once more at grain fill if May turns dry. Three waterings total counting the winter one. Pumping costs maybe 40 yuan each time per mu — adds up fast.

Spray herbicide once in early spring for the weeds, and if I see rust or powdery mildew around heading I'll spray fungicide. If not, I save the money.

Harvest around June 8 or 9. I hire the combine, 80 yuan a mu. Last year I got 420 kg per mu. I expect about the same — 400 to 430 if weather is ordinary.

**Maize (5 mu) — right after wheat**

This is the tight part. Once the combine's gone through, I've got maybe 4-5 days. I hire the no-till planter — the guy from the neighboring village runs his machine through ours. He charges by the mu. No tilling, drops seed right into the wheat stubble. That's how everyone does it now. Saves time, saves fuel.

Zhengdan 958 seed, about 70 yuan a mu. The planter drops compound fertilizer in the row with the seed — one bag per mu again. At big trumpet stage, late July, I topdress urea by hand, maybe 15-20 kg per mu.

Water depends on the sky. If July rains come, I might not irrigate at all. Usually I end up watering once or twice during the dry stretch. Spray herbicide early, that's about it for chemicals unless the armyworm shows up.

Combine harvest end of September, early October. Last year 470 kg per mu. Expecting similar.

**Cotton (2.8 mu) — planting mid-late April**

Cotton's more trouble than grain but it pays OK. I bought seed already — Bt variety from the shop in town, about 50 yuan a mu. I'll rototill the strip, lay mulch film, and plant by hand with the wife.

One bag of compound at planting. Then urea twice — about 10 kg per mu at squaring, another 10 kg at flowering. Cotton's thirsty and drinks more than maize. I'll irrigate twice, maybe three times if June-July is dry.

Cotton needs more spraying than grain — bollworm, aphids, spider mites, maybe fungus in a wet year. I spray 4 or 5 times through the season. Chemicals run maybe 150 yuan a mu.

Picking starts early September, three or four rounds into October. My wife and I do it. If my oldest son can come back from town on weekends he helps. Last year I got around 240 kg of lint per mu. Cotton price was decent — hope it holds.

**Money**

Adds up to roughly 7,000-7,200 yuan across the whole farm for the year. I've got that from last year's sales plus what the kids send home. Not borrowing this year, which I prefer. I borrowed one year back when my youngest was still in school and I didn't like owing the coop.

**What could go wrong**

If May-June turns dry, wheat grain fill gets hurt and I'll water a fourth time — costly but worth it, you don't skimp on wheat water at grain fill. If cotton price drops by autumn, that strip doesn't pay and I'll feel it. If my son can't come help pick cotton, we hire one day-laborer for a few days, around 120 yuan a day. We manage.
